title: Comparing Surgical and Nonsurgical Outcomes of Tennis Elbow
official: Nonoperative vs. Surgical Release for Acute-to-Subacute Lateral Epicondylitis: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Tennis elbow is a condition that causes pain on the outside of the elbow, typically caused by motions involving straightening of the arm. The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate whether early surgery leads to better outcomes than physical therapy and watchful waiting for tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis) in adults. This study aims to answer the following questions:

* Does earlier surgical intervention improve pain and function more than physical therapy and watchful waiting after one year?
* How do symptoms and function compare between the two treatments over two years?
* How often do people who start with physical therapy and watchful waiting end up needing surgery?

Researchers will compare early surgery to physical therapy and watchful waiting to see which treatment works better.

Participants will...

* be randomly assigned to have surgery or to try physical therapy and watchful waiting.
* have a physical exam and grip strength test at each visit.
* answer questionnaires about their elbow pain and function.
* attend appointments at the start of the study, and at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Clinical diagnosis of lateral epicondylitis, defined by:

  * Lateral elbow pain reproduced by resisted wrist extension or resisted middle finger extension
  * Tenderness to palpation over the lateral epicondyle or common extensor origin
* Symptom duration of at least 2 weeks and no more than 3 months at time of enrollment
* Willing and able to comply with follow-up schedule and assigned treatment protocol
* Able to provide written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior surgery on the ipsilateral elbow
* Prior corticosteroid or biologic (PRP, autologous blood) injection to the ipsilateral lateral epicondyle within 3 months of enrollment
* Concomitant ipsilateral elbow pathology (e.g., posterolateral rotatory instability, radial tunnel syndrome, intra-articular pathology, medial epicondylitis)
* Cervical radiculopathy or other proximal source of referred lateral elbow pain
* Active elbow fracture or acute traumatic injury to the affected extremity
* Inflammatory arthropathy affecting the elbow (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, gout)
* Pregnancy
* Inability to comply with follow-up visits or complete patient-reported outcome instruments
* Concurrent participation in another interventional study affecting upper extremity function
